analysis.title: EMEA investors should look at home and abroad to build resilience (UBS House View - Daily EMEA)
key_insights: UBS says EMEA investors may find resilience by combining selected home-region assets with return sources from further afield, without adopting a narrow home bias, because 2027 is expected to have an unusually wide range of outcomes.

UBS rates fixed income Attractive and favors intermediate duration (maturities of about two to 10 years). Quality bonds give income and diversification if equity volatility rises, while EM and high yield bonds offer greater return potential.

EM sovereign bonds yield about 7.1%, EM corporate bonds about 7.0% and US high yield about 8.3%. In European credit UBS favors medium-maturity A- and BBB-rated issuers (utilities, infrastructure, telecoms, energy, banks) and says to limit the longest maturities, weak borrowers and issuers with large refinancing needs.

Eurozone is UBS's preferred equity region. It expects 15% earnings growth in 2027, matching its US forecast, from a lower starting valuation and with less dependence on AI-linked companies. It also favors banks, information technology, utilities and Germany, and is selective on consumer sectors because of weak Chinese demand.

UBS expects broad commodities to benefit from structural investment in power, electrification, data centers and supply chain resilience, and recommends an actively managed allocation across energy, industrial metals, agriculture and gold. A conventional oil-and-gas-heavy commodity index may reinforce, not diversify, Middle Eastern investors' existing exposure.

UBS favors hedge fund strategies that exploit dispersion (low-net and market-neutral equity, merger arbitrage, fixed income relative value, discretionary macro, multi-strategy). In private markets it favors operationally focused PE, middle-market and complex transactions, secondaries, and core/core-plus infrastructure. It flags long lockups, uncertain capital calls, leverage, fees and opaque valuations as risks.

Sterling is UBS's preferred G10 carry currency, supported by resilient UK activity and a yield advantage over the euro and Swiss franc, with fiscal credibility as the main risk. It also sees opportunities in EM carry: South African rand, Mexican peso, Brazilian real and Indian rupee.

The minutes of the Fed's 27-28 October meeting show almost all officials expected further rate increases to be appropriate. Two participants said a move larger than 25bp could be warranted in December if inflation data is unfavorable. Officials called price pressures broad-based and named AI-related demand as a material inflation risk.
UBS expects the Fed to raise rates in December and again in March 2027. It says further hikes are largely priced in and that cumulative tightening should limit the need for a prolonged hiking cycle.

3-month LME copper fell 5.7% on Wednesday to USD 12,471/mt, the lowest since April and more than 10% below its peak. Drivers cited were AI growth concerns, Fed tightening weighing on demand and skepticism over potential US tariffs on refined copper.

UBS attributes the copper drop to weaker sentiment and rising exchange inventories, not weaker fundamentals. It cites disappointing mine-supply growth, deeply negative treatment charges and robust electrification and grid demand. It stays constructive, views weakness as a chance to add, and keeps a USD 15,500/mt forecast by mid-2027.

The S&P 500 Managed Health Care Index fell nearly 14% from Monday's close after CMS proposed tighter Medicare Advantage risk-adjustment oversight (CMS estimates savings of almost USD 90bn over 10 years), alongside Democratic senators' criticism of insurers and renewed talk of expanding Medicare.

UBS sees negligible effects on industry earnings over the next two years. It expects possible litigation delays, thinks Medicare-for-All is highly unlikely in the next Congress, and calls the sell-off a reassessment of benign policy expectations and positioning. It sees managed care valuations as reasonable but expects more policy-driven volatility toward the 2028 election.

sector_views.rationale: Preferred equity region, 15% expected 2027 earnings growth from a lower starting valuation and less AI concentration.
Defense, infrastructure, automation, power networks and electrification investment should support earnings.
Provides a less cyclical earnings stream.
Favored in Europe. Utilities offer exposure to rising electricity demand and ballast if growth disappoints.
UBS wants to stay selective because weak Chinese demand remains a risk.
UBS sees negligible earnings effect from the CMS proposal over two years and reasonable valuations, but expects more policy-driven volatility.
Structural investment in power, electrification, data centers and supply chain resilience, with each segment giving a different return driver.

earnings_insights: UBS forecasts 15% earnings growth in 2027 for both the Eurozone and the US (house forecast, not a reported figure).
UBS expects negligible effects on US health insurer industry earnings over the next two years from the CMS Medicare Advantage proposal (UBS estimate).

trade_ideas.description: Add copper exposure on weakness as part of an actively managed broad commodity allocation
trade_ideas.rationale: Mine-supply growth is disappointing, treatment charges are deeply negative and electrification and grid demand are robust.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker sentiment, rising exchange inventories, Fed tightening and potential US tariffs on refined copper.

trade_ideas.description: Long sterling as the preferred G10 carry currency versus euro and Swiss franc
trade_ideas.rationale: Resilient UK activity and a yield advantage over the euro and Swiss franc.

trade_ideas.description: Diversified emerging market carry via South African rand, Mexican peso, Brazilian real and Indian rupee
trade_ideas.rationale: The report cites opportunities in diversified EM carry.

trade_ideas.description: Intermediate-duration fixed income (2-10 year maturities) with quality bonds, plus EM and high yield bonds for return
trade_ideas.rationale: Elevated starting yields give income and a cushion, and quality bonds would rally if risks intensify.
trade_ideas.risk: Yields could rise further if the Fed hikes more than expected.

risk_factors: Elevated AI expectations, questions over AI monetization and AI concentration in major equity indexes.
AI-related demand as a material inflation risk, and financial vulnerabilities from rapidly growing AI debt, complex financing structures, elevated valuations and hedge fund leverage.
A Fed hike larger than 25bp in December if inflation data is unfavorable, and consecutive hikes.
Weak Chinese demand for European consumer sectors.
Copper: rising exchange inventories, Fed tightening, potential US refined copper tariffs.
US managed care: policy headlines, Medicare Advantage rule uncertainty, and volatility into the 2028 election.
Alternatives: long lockups, uncertain capital calls, leverage, high fees, limited transparency and subjective valuations.
vol_and_positioning: UBS says quality bonds would likely rally and insulate portfolios if equity volatility rises or economic and equity market risks intensify.
Hedge fund leverage and elevated asset valuations were discussed in the Fed minutes as financial vulnerabilities.
UBS attributes the managed care sell-off partly to investor positioning.
geopolitical: Potential Trump administration tariffs on refined copper weigh on copper sentiment.
Close of the APEC summit is listed among the items to watch on 19 November.
Geopolitical disruption is cited as a reason to hold energy within commodities, and 2027 is expected to have an unusually wide range of geopolitical outcomes.
Weak Chinese demand is cited as a risk to European consumer sectors.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS says further hikes are largely priced in and cumulative tightening plus tighter financial conditions should limit the need for a prolonged cycle, so quality bonds keep their income and cushion.
tension_points.bear_case: Fed minutes show almost all officials expect more hikes, two see a larger-than-25bp move possible in December, and officials call price pressures broad-based with AI demand as a material inflation risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Unfavorable inflation data that prompts a larger-than-25bp December hike or consecutive moves.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS says weakness is sentiment and inventory driven while mine supply disappoints, treatment charges are deeply negative and electrification demand is robust, supporting USD 15,500/mt by mid-2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Copper fell 5.7% amid AI growth concerns, Fed tightening weighing on demand, rising exchange inventories and skepticism over potential US refined copper tariffs.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS sees negligible earnings effects over two years, likely litigation delays, a very unlikely Medicare expansion and reasonable valuations.
tension_points.bear_case: The index fell nearly 14% since Monday on CMS Medicare Advantage oversight proposals and criticism from Democratic senators, with policy headlines driving more volatility toward the 2028 election.
